name: VibeVoice-ASR
purpose: Unified long-form speech-to-text that outputs who spoke, when and what in one pass, with custom hotwords; up to 60 minutes continuous audio within a 64K token window (card).

license.name: MIT
license.notes: LICENSE in https://github.com/microsoft/VibeVoice read: MIT License, Copyright (c) 2025 Microsoft.

architecture.kind: AUTOREGRESSIVE: Qwen2-based 28-layer dense decoder (hidden 3584, 28 heads, 4 KV heads, full attention) with causal acoustic (64-dim) and semantic (128-dim) tokenizers at about 15 frames per second (assumes 24 kHz) and a diffusion head in the config

pc-16gb.notes: Q4 weights about 5-6 GB; a 60 min file is about 54k tokens, KV 28 layers x 4 heads x 128 x 2 x 2 B = 57 KB/token, about 3 GB; no quantized runtime known

engine_support.notes: Plain Qwen2 decoder: Tona's dense-transformer path could in principle serve it; the convolutional audio tokenizers would need ports.

strengths: ASR, diarization and timestamps in one 60-minute pass, no stitching
weaknesses: German not named in the card text, the language chart is an image
No numeric benchmarks in card text, no VRAM or speed figures

user_reports.summary: Inference can spiral into repeating one word or phrase until the token limit; still reproducible in October with noisy speech; a client script (PR 228) covers only the vLLM server.

tona_fit.reason: Unique feature (one pass: who, when, what, hotwords, 60 min) and MIT, but the independent German WER is poor (14.12 on all 8 sets, rank 26 of 27) and long-form loops are reported. Dense Qwen2-7B-class decoder would suit Tona, and 16 GB is marginal at best. Revisit if a later checkpoint fixes German.

open_questions: Speed (tokens per audio second) and VRAM at 60 min
Whether the decoder equals Qwen2.5-7B (config: qwen2, 28 layers, hidden 3584)

benchmarks.name: German WER, Open ASR multilingual track (8 of 8 datasets)
benchmarks.harness: Open ASR Leaderboard multilingual track, German column (WER %), read from the Space config JSON 2026-11-19; rows differ in how many of the 8 datasets they cover
